question: Which filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this issue: PathGuard-style allow/deny paths, roots with access modes, a narrower workspace-only/exec-split design, or no native host path ACL beyond existing sandboxing?
rationale: The issue defines a public config and security boundary, and current open implementation candidates make different tradeoffs around API shape, compatibility, exec coverage, and false-security risk.

options.title: Choose one canonical tools.fs path-policy contract
options.body: Settle the API shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.

options.title: Split exec into a separate security tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state shell-mediated filesystem access remains a separate boundary.

options.title: Reject native host path ACLs for now
options.body: Keep OS users, containers, and existing workspaceOnly/sandbox backends as the supported hard boundary and close or downgrade this config request.

recommendation.title: Choose one canonical tools.fs path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Settle the API shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.
